title: City Transport Policy
description: Your city council advisory committee must recommend the transport initiative that will anchor the next 5-year capital plan. Public pressure is high: commuters want relief, neighbourhood groups are watching the equity impacts, and councillors need a proposal that can survive scrutiny after the announcement. Review the evidence and make a recommendation.
p1_persona: You are a community impact advisor to the council. Your focus is access, seasonal usefulness, social equity, and whether the initiative improves everyday mobility for residents who rely on public infrastructure.
p2_persona: You are an infrastructure delivery advisor to the council. Your focus is construction risk, legal exposure, cost control, and whether the initiative can be delivered within the political and budget window.
correct_rationale: Pooled, Light Rail (A) has fatal flaws (P2: heritage-zone delays, twice-revised cost overruns, lowest projected ridership) and Cycling (C) has fatal flaws (P1: 60% winter usage drop, no impact on commuter routes, equity-of-access gap). Electric BRT has only mild operational drawbacks. BRT wins by elimination.
shared_info: The Light Rail Extension covers 12km of new track at $850M total cost
Electric Bus Rapid Transit covers 45km of dedicated bus lanes at $280M total cost
The Cycling Infrastructure Network covers 200km of protected bike lanes at $120M total cost
p1_unique_info: The Cycling Network's projected usage drops 60% during the city's 5-month winter season — making peak-season ridership numbers misleading
The Cycling Network would not serve the four outer suburbs where the city's lowest-income workers live, raising significant equity-of-access concerns flagged by the social policy committee
Independent transport modelling shows the Cycling Network would have negligible impact on commuter routes — only 2.1% modal shift from cars to bikes
Electric BRT requires a fleet replacement cycle every 8 years, locking in ongoing capital costs
Electric BRT shares lanes with emergency vehicles in some corridors, requiring careful traffic-management coordination
The Electric BRT vehicle vendor is based overseas — parts lead times average 6 weeks
p2_unique_info: The Light Rail Extension route passes through a contested heritage zone that has blocked 2 previous infrastructure projects — legal challenges are virtually certain
The Light Rail Extension's cost estimate has already been revised upward twice during the planning phase, from $600M to $850M, with consultants warning of a third revision
Independent transport modelling shows Light Rail would serve only 45,000 daily riders — the lowest projected ridership of the three options
Electric BRT's 18-month construction window will require partial closures of two arterial roads, with projected commuter delays of 8–12 minutes during peak
Electric BRT's electricity demand will require minor grid upgrades at 3 substations, adding ~$8M to the project cost
Electric BRT vehicles cost 30% more to maintain in their first year than projected, based on data from the early-adopter cities
anchor_rationale: Light Rail is a premium transit option that signals the city's ambition
